questions.question:
Which two signs need to be interchanged to make the following equation correct?

9 + 3 − 4 ÷ 5 × 2 = 9
questions.solution:
Given equation: 9 + 3 − 4 ÷ 5 × 2 = 9.

BODMAS Table: 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/d50192f098c21078501d30eeafe1a8c64bc30dd9621c48caa8a39ffc60f68b64.png] 

Let's check each option one by one.

Option 1) − and ×

Given: 9 + 3 − 4 ÷ 5 × 2 = 9

After interchanging the numbers we get;

⇒ 9 + 3 × __**4 ÷ 5**__ - 2 = 9

⇒ 9 + __**3 × 0.8**__ - 2 = 9

⇒ __**9 + 2.4**__ - 2 = 9

⇒ __**11.4 - 2**__ = 9

⇒ 9.4 ≠ 9

⇒ LHS ≠ RHS

Option 2) + and x

Given: 9 + 3 − 4 ÷ 5 × 2 = 9

After interchanging the numbers we get;

⇒ 9 × 3 − __**4 ÷ 5**__ + 2 = 9

⇒ __**9 ×**__**__ 3__ **− 0.8 + 2 = 9

⇒ __27__ - 0.8 + __**2**__ = 9

⇒ __29____ - 0.8__ = 9

⇒ 28.2 ≠ 9

⇒ LHS ≠ RHS

**Option 3) + and ÷**

Given: 9 + 3 − 4 ÷ 5 × 2 = 9

After interchanging the numbers we get;

⇒ __**9 ÷ 3**__ − 4 + 5 × 2 = 9

⇒ 3 − 4 + __**5 × 2**__ = 9

⇒ __**3**__ − 4 __**+ 10**__ = 9

⇒ __**13 - 4**__ = 9

⇒ __**9 = 9**__

⇒ **LHS = RHS**

Option 4) − and +

Given: 9 + 3 − 4 ÷ 5 × 2 = 9

After interchanging the numbers we get;

⇒ 9 - 3 + __**4 ÷ 5**__ × 2 = 9

⇒ 9 - 3 + __**0.8 × 2**__ = 9

⇒ __**9**__ - 3 + __**1.6**__ = 9

⇒ __**10.6 -**____** 3**__ = 9

⇒ 7.6 ≠ 9

⇒ LHS ≠ RHS

Hence, the correct answer is "Option 3".

questions.question: 80 liters of a mixture of alcohol and water contains 60% alcohol. If 'X' liters of water is added to this mixture, then the percentage of alcohol in the new mixture becomes 40%. What is the value of 'X'?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Since **water** is added, the quantity of **alcohol** remains **constant**.

Ratio of Alcohol Concentration (Initial : New) = 60% : 40% = 3 : 2

Ratio of **Total Mixture** volume is inversely proportional to concentration = 2 : 3

Initial 2 units = 80 liters ⇒ 1 unit = 40 liters

Added water (X) = Increase in volume = 3 − 2 = 1 unit = 40

**∴ The correct answer is 40.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Initial Volume = 80 liters | Alcohol % = 60% | Final Alcohol % = 40%

**Formula Used:**

Amount of Alcohol = (Alcohol % / 100) × Total Mixture Volume

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c4900d12bbbfe5c382c55dec13c96e5e82030b49d3051fe1d326bd56b9288103.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Quantity of **Alcohol** in initial mixture = 60% of 80 = (60/100) × 80 = 48 liters

⇒ Let **X** liters of water be added. Total volume of new mixture = (80 + X) liters

⇒ In the new mixture, **Alcohol** is 40% of the total volume.

⇒ 40% of (80 + X) = 48

⇒ (40/100) × (80 + X) = 48

⇒ 0.4 × (80 + X) = 48

⇒ 80 + X = 48 / 0.4 = 120

⇒ X = 120 − 80 = 40

**∴ The correct answer is 40.**

**__Additional Information__**

Constant Quantity Rule

When one component (like water) is added to a mixture, the amount of the other component (like alcohol) remains unchanged in weight or volume.

Dilution Formula

For any solution, C₁V₁ = C₂V₂, where C is concentration and V is total volume of the mixture.

Alligation Method

Ratio of (Mixture A : Pure Water) = (Concentration of Water in Final − Concentration of Water Added) : (Concentration of Alcohol Initial − Concentration of Alcohol Final).</p

questions.question: Akshay has 30 articles, each having the same cost price. He marked the price of each article at 30% above its cost price. He sold 15 of the articles at a discount of 20% each, and the remaining 15 articles at a discount of 10% each, thereby gaining a total profit of Rs. 630. What was the cost price of each article?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Assume **Cost Price (CP)** of each article is 100 units → **Marked Price (MP)** = 130 units.

**Case 1:** 15 articles at 20% discount on MP → SP₁ = 130 − 26 = 104 units → **Profit** = 4 units/article.

**Case 2:** 15 articles at 10% discount on MP → SP₂ = 130 − 13 = 117 units → **Profit** = 17 units/article.

Total units of profit = (15 × 4) + (15 × 17) = 60 + 255 = 315 units.

Actual Profit Rs. 630 → 315 units = 630 → 1 unit = Rs. 2 ∴ 100 units = Rs. 200.

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 200.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Total articles = 30, **Markup** = 30%, **Total Profit** = Rs. 630.

**Formula Used:** Selling Price (SP) = CP + Profit | SP = MP × (100 − Discount)%

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/146b3fc3edc2bf837623c5173b4987f807dc8a619f234193ef8ed6eec101ea4b.png] 

Let the **Cost Price (CP)** of each article be x.

⇒ **Marked Price (MP)** = x + 30% of x = 1.3x

⇒ **Selling Price** of first 15 articles (SP₁) = 1.3x × (100 − 20)% = 1.3x × 0.8 = 1.04x

⇒ **Selling Price** of remaining 15 articles (SP₂) = 1.3x × (100 − 10)% = 1.3x × 0.9 = 1.17x

⇒ **Total Selling Price** = (15 × 1.04x) + (15 × 1.17x)

⇒ **Total Cost Price** = 30x

⇒ **Total Profit** = Total SP − Total CP = 630

⇒ 15.6x + 17.55x − 30x = 630

⇒ 33.15x − 30x = 630

⇒ 3.15x = 630

⇒ x = 630 ÷ 3.15 = 200

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 200.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Markup and Discount Relationship

Profit % = Markup % − Discount % − (Markup × Discount)/100. This is derived from the successive percentage change formula.

Selling Price Formula

SP = CP × (1 + Profit%/100) or SP = MP × (1 − Discount%/100). Both can be used to equate and find unknown variables.

Marked Price Ratio

MP/CP = (100 + Profit%)/(100 − Discount%). This ratio helps find the markup required for a specific profit after a given discount.</p

• Bryophytes:

 
 
• In the plant kingdom, bryophytes are known as amphibians.
 
• A bryophyte is a nonvascular plant that is green, seedless and belongs to the mosses, liverworts, or hornworts family.
 
• Bryophytes are among the simplest of terrestrial plants.
 
• In Bryophyta, there is a lack of xylem and phloem tissue.
 
• They lack true roots, stem and leaves.
 
• Bryophytes are known as the amphibians of the plant kingdom because they live in the soil but need water to reproduce sexually.
 
• They prefer moist, humid, and shady environments.

• They reproduce with the help of spores formed along the back or posterior surface of their leaves.
 
• Examples - ferns like Nephrolepis, Marsilea, Pteris, Adiantum, Equisetum, Selaginella, Lycopodium, etc.
 
 
 
 

 Angiosperms

• The word Angiosperms is made from two Greek words: Angio which means covered and Sperma which means seed.
 
• Plant seeds having two cotyledons are called dicots.

__
 
• Buddha attained enlightenment at Bodh Gaya in Bihar.
 
• He attained enlightenment under a peepal tree at Bodh Gaya where he meditated for days.
 
• After attaining enlightenment, he came to be known as Buddha or the wise one.
 
• The day Gautam Buddha attained enlightenment is celebrated as Buddha Purnima. 
 
• The exact date of is based on the Asian lunisolar calendars and is primarily celebrated in Baisakh month. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Buddha had instructed his followers to cremate his body as the body of a universal monarch would be cremated and then to distribute the relics among various groups of his lay followers, who were to enshrine them in hemispherical reliquaries called stupas.
 
• His body lay in a coffin for seven days before being placed on a funeral pyre and was set ablaze by the Buddha’s chief disciple, Mahakashyapa, who had been absent at the time of the Buddha’s death.
 
• After the Buddha’s cremation, his relics were entrusted to a group of lay disciples, but armed men arrived from seven other regions and demanded the relics. In order to avert bloodshed, a monk divided the relics into eight portions.
 
• According to tradition, 10 sets of relics were enshrined, 8 from portions of the Buddha’s remains, 1 from the pyre’s ashes, and 1 from the bucket used to divide the remains.
 
• The stupa (“stupa” is Sanskrit for heap) is an important form of Buddhist architecture, though it predates Buddhism. The custom of rearing stupas was pre-Buddhist. 
 
• A stupa is a dirt burial mound faced with stone. In Buddhism, the earliest stupas contained portions of the Buddha’s ashes, and as a result, the stupa began to be associated with the body of the Buddha.

• Chaitya was a rectangular prayer hall with a stupa placed in the centre, the purpose was prayer.

• The central part of the hall (also called the nave) was separated from the two aisles by two rows of pillars.
 
• The chaityas also had polished interior walls, semicircular roofs and horse-shoe-shaped windows called the Chaitya windows.
 
• Viharas were the residences of the monks.

• The temple has a massive collonaded prakara (corridor) and is one of the largest Shiva lingams in India. It is also famed for the quality of its sculpture.

questions.question: Which state of India has set up District Investment Promotion Agencies (DIPA)?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Odisha**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In a bid to promote and facilitate investment across the State, the Odisha government__ has announced the setting up of District Investment Promotion Agencies (DIPAs) in 30 districts. 
 
• DIPA shall operate under the leadership of the respective District Collector with other s**enior district officials including SPs, DFOs and line Department officials being constituent members.**
 
• The District Collector shall be supported by a team of professionals for investment facilitation, project monitoring and promoting local entrepreneurship.
 
• The DIPAs will work as an extended arm of the Industrial Promotion and **Investment Corporation of Odisha (IPICOL) **and will be set up in phases from **April 2021 to December 2021.**
 
• The performance of DIPAs will be monitored by State Level Single Window Clearance Authority and will also be evaluated through annual rankings of districts based on investor feedback.
